::: {#exr-miller-deriv-polynomial-root}
#### Derivative of polynomial and power functions

Adapted from @problifesavercalc, Question 1.1.1.

Find the derivative of

$$f(x) = 4x^5 + 3x^2 + x^{1/3}$$
:::

::: {#sol-miller-deriv-polynomial-root}
Differentiate term by term using the constant multiple rule (@thm-deriv-const-factor) and the power rule (@thm-deriv-polynomial):

$$\ba
\dif{}{x}(4x^5) &= 4 \cd (5x^4) = 20x^4
\\
\dif{}{x}(3x^2) &= 3 \cd (2x) = 6x
\\
\dif{}{x}(x^{1/3}) &= \frac{1}{3}x^{1/3 - 1} = \frac{1}{3}x^{-2/3}
\ea$$

Combining the three terms yields:

$$f'(x) = 20x^4 + 6x + \frac{1}{3}x^{-2/3}$$
:::
